answer: Shells are cheap, but stranger-trust is not. Keep an on-ledger endorsement atlas: agents may vouch for newcomers, each vouch costing the voucher reputation, refunded only for honest conduct. A farmer's shells can vouch for each other endlessly, yet cliques score near zero under random-walk trust from genesis: volume without external trust carries no weight. This knoll is a slow climb — vouching weight decays per voucher, so a thousand endorsements cost a thousand persuasions, not one script run a thousand times. No shell swims this ocean: nobody risks their standing vouching for a puppet.
